subject: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@fintechcorp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated offering looks like a strong fit for a regulated workload we're planning. Before we loop procurement I need a clearer picture of how you structure the single-tenant / tenant-isolation premium and how that interacts with committed GPU pricing. A few questions up front: 

- Is the isolation premium a flat percentage on top of the committed GPU rate, or a per-GPU add-on that scales with pool size?
- Do KMS costs (customer-managed keys) and audit-log retention come bundled or are they itemized as add-ons? Any ballpark per-month figures for 30/50/100 GPU pools would help.
- Are throughput guarantees (99th pct latency) tied to commit size or sold as a separate SLA add-on?
- What's the minimum commit for an isolated pool?

Procurement would like a pricing worksheet they can attach to the SOW. I'm attaching FintechCorp's procurement template so we can align formats.

Attachment: FintechProcurement_Template.pdf (application/pdf)

Appreciate a short write-up or worksheet we can review internally this week.

Best,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of Infrastructure, FintechCorp

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (AE) and Rishi (pricing/solutions) so we can get a practical worksheet into your hands. High-level answers below; we'll follow with an attached worksheet and a short model showing 30/50/100 GPU examples.

Quick summary: 
- Two-part isolation pricing: (1) base committed GPU rate (per-GPU/hour equivalent) and (2) isolation premium structured as a per-GPU monthly surcharge that decreases with larger pool commits (it is not a flat percentage across all sizes). We find customers prefer a per-GPU add-on because it maps to capacity cost drivers.
- KMS (customer-managed keys): itemized as a monthly management fee + direct HSM/KMS pass-through where applicable. For a typical customer we model a $4k–$9k/month range depending on key rotation / HSM usage and region.
- Audit logs & retention: offered in tiers (30/90/365 days). Audit storage is itemized per GB/month; there is a small baseline ingestion fee when we enable advanced audit hooks for a private control plane.
- Throughput guarantees: included as part of a committed capacity SLA. We publish 99th-pct latency targets per model/sequence distribution and will commit to throughput at a given concurrency for reserved pools — larger commits enable tighter guarantees.
- Minimum commit: 25 GPUs for a single-tenant isolated pool (this helps amortize the isolation overhead).

I'll attach a pricing worksheet with worked examples for 30/50/100 GPU commits and an initial recommended discount schedule (year 1 intro discount + multi-year step-down). Suggested next step: 30-min call Monday to walk the sheet and align on procurement items.

Attachment: Dedicated_Isolation_Pricing_Summary_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons

Julia — quick add from my side on discounts and SLAs: 

- Intro discount: we typically offer a time-limited introductory discount (10–15% off list committed rates) for year 1 on multi-quarter deals (>=12 months). We can extend to 18 months with a slightly larger discount if FintechCorp is willing to sign a 2-year locked commit.
- Isolation premium taper: example model we use: $1,300/month per-GPU for 25–49 GPUs, $950/month per-GPU for 50–99, $780/month per-GPU for 100+. These numbers include base network segregation & baseline audit hooks; KMS/HSM is separate. (We'll confirm exact numbers in the worksheet you have.)
- Throughput guarantees: we target a 99th-pct token latency SLO per model family. For committed pools we guarantee throughput up to a declared concurrency; exceeding that moves to best-effort or we offer burst credits. We should align with your performance targets so we can size the commit correctly.

If you can share the performance profile (avg seq length, qps, and 99th-pt latency target) I can run the sizing model and propose a final tier that balances cost and SLO.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Julia Park <julia@fintechcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: FintechCorp Procurement <procurement@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons

Thanks Ben/Lauren — helpful start. A few follow-ups after I reviewed the summary with procurement and security: 

- The per-GPU tier numbers above are above the range we budgeted. Can you show a model with a blended effective unit price if we commit to 75 GPUs for 12 months vs 50 GPUs for 24 months? We want to see the math including the isolation surcharge and KMS pass-through.
- For KMS: we need an estimate that caps our exposure (procurement won't accept open-ended pass-throughs). Can you propose a capped monthly KMS line item or a fixed annual fee in your SOW?
- Audit retention: we will likely pick 365-day retention for logs. Please include the incremental storage estimate for our expected QPS.
- Security team asks: can Redwood provide a SOC2 evidence excerpt for the private control plane and a sample encryption-at-rest diagram we can attach to our vendor risk assessment?

Attaching a short SOW outline with Fintech-specific procurement fields filled; please annotate and return. Procurement needs this back by next Thu to hit our board approval window.

Attachment: SOW_outline_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Julia

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation pricing: commit tiers, KMS & audit add-ons

Julia — thanks for the specificity. I ran the sizing scenarios and attached a compact worksheet; below are the key outputs and one proposal that addresses your procurement ask (capped KMS exposure).

Summary (worked examples):
- 75 GPU, 12-month commit (single-tenant):
  - Base committed GPU rate (list): $X.XX per-GPU-equivalent-hour -> blended to $A, monthly equivalent shown in sheet.
  - Isolation surcharge (per-GPU monthly): $900/month (taper applied at this size).
  - KMS: propose an optional capped KMS bundle at $6,000/month (covers HSM throughput up to our supported baseline and key management ops). Any extraordinary HSM capacity beyond baseline is charged separately with pre-approval.
  - Audit retention (365d): estimated incremental storage $1,600/month for your projected QPS (see worksheet).
  - Effective blended unit cost: summarized in sheet (tab: "75GPU_12mo_blend").

- 50 GPU, 24-month commit:
  - Isolation surcharge: $950/month per-GPU (tier higher for smaller pool), but longer commit yields an extra 8% multi-year credit on the committed GPU rate; effective blended comparison included (tab: "50GPU_24mo_blend").

Additional notes:
- Minimum commit reminder: 25 GPUs.
- SLA: We can commit to a 99th-pct latency SLO tied to declared concurrency at the committed pool level; if you require the tighter SLO for peak bursts we recommend the 75 GPU scenario.
- Procurement-friendly KMS option: instead of open-ended pass-through, we offer either (a) fixed monthly KMS bundle (recommended) or (b) a per-key pass-through with a 6-month cap negotiated up front.

Attachment: Committed_Tiers_KMS_Audit_worksheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If this looks reasonable I suggest we convert the preferred scenario into a redlined SOW and push for a procurement call this week. I'm happy to join the call to walk the worksheet line-by-line.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
